hear.creation:
It is the beginning of the world. There is no sun yet, no trees, no people. The earth is without form, and dark, and the Spirit of God moves on the face of the waters.
God said, Let there be light, and there was light. He divided the light from the darkness, and called the light Day. He made a firmament and called it Heaven. He gathered the waters so dry land appeared, and called it Earth, and the waters Seas, and it was good. He made grass and herbs and fruit trees. He made two great lights, the sun to rule the day and the moon to rule the night, and He made the stars also. He filled the waters with living creatures and the sky with fowl, and He blessed them. He made cattle and creeping things and beasts of the earth. Then God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness, and God created man in His own image, male and female. He blessed them and gave them the earth to dress. God saw every thing that He had made. On the seventh day He ended His work, and He rested, and blessed that day.
“And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.” Genesis 1:31.
God made everything good — including you.
hear.baby-moses:
Egypt. A river with tall reeds. Pharaoh has ordered that Hebrew baby boys must not live. One mother will not give her child up.
She hid him three months. When she could hide him no longer, she made an ark of bulrushes, daubed it with slime and pitch, put the child in, and laid it in the flags by the river’s brink. His sister stood afar off to see what would be done. Pharaoh’s daughter came down to wash, saw the ark, opened it, and the babe wept. She had compassion, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children. The sister asked if she should call a nurse of the Hebrew women. Pharaoh’s daughter said yes — and the nurse was the baby’s own mother, paid to raise him. When the child grew, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She called his name Moses, because she drew him out of the water. God was already writing a deliverance before Moses could walk.
“She called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.” Exodus 2:10.
God watches over little ones.
hear.moses-red-sea:
A shore at the edge of the sea. Behind God’s people is Pharaoh’s army. In front is water. There is no path that looks safe.
The LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand. Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he pursued them with chariots. The people were sore afraid and cried to Moses. Moses said, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD. The angel of God and the pillar of the cloud stood between Israel and the Egyptians. The LORD told Moses to lift up his rod and stretch out his hand over the sea. Moses did, and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided. The children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground, the waters a wall on the right and on the left. The Egyptians followed. Moses stretched out his hand again, the sea returned, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore. They believed the LORD, and His servant Moses.
“Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.” Exodus 14:13.
God makes a way when there seems none.
hear.jonah:
A port called Joppa. God has spoken. Jonah does not want to go.
The word of the LORD came to Jonah, Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it. Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD. He paid the fare and went down into the ship. The LORD sent out a great wind, and there was a mighty tempest, so that the ship was like to be broken. The mariners were afraid. They cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah. He said, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea. They did, and the sea ceased from her raging. The LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights. Jonah prayed. The LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land. The word of the LORD came the second time, and Jonah went to Nineveh. He cried, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. So the people of Nineveh believed God, from the greatest of them even to the least of them, and God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way.
“And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.” Jonah 2:10.
God’s mercy reaches farther than we run.
hear.noah:
A world that has grown violent. God is grieved. One man still walks with Him.
God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth. But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD. God said, Make thee an ark of gopher wood. Rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and pitch it within and without. Noah did according to all that God commanded him. They went in, two and two of all flesh, and Noah’s wife, and his sons, and his sons’ wives with him. The rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights. The waters increased, and bare up the ark, and all flesh died that moved upon the earth. God remembered Noah, and every living thing that was with him in the ark. The waters asswaged. Noah sent forth a raven, then a dove. The dove came in with an olive leaf. God said, Go forth of the ark. Noah builded an altar. God set His bow in the cloud, for a token of a covenant between Him and the earth, that the waters should no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
“And God remembered Noah.” Genesis 8:1.
God keeps His promises.
hear.david:
Two hills, a valley between. On one side Israel. On the other the Philistines. A giant named Goliath walks out and shouts.
He was six cubits and a span, with a helmet of brass and a coat of mail. He defied the armies of Israel forty days. Saul and all Israel were dismayed. David was a shepherd, the youngest of Jesse. He had been keeping sheep. He came to the camp with food for his brothers and heard the giant. David said, Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? Saul put his armour on David, but David put it off. He took his staff, five smooth stones out of the brook, and his sling. Goliath cursed him. David said, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts. He ran toward the Philistine, slung a stone, and smote him in the forehead. The stone sunk into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the earth. David prevailed with a sling and with a stone. Israel rose and shouted.
“The battle is the LORD's.” 1 Samuel 17:47.
God is bigger than the loudest fear.
hear.jesus-children:
A road with Jesus. People have brought little children so He might touch them. The disciples think the children are in the way.
They brought young children to Him, that He should touch them: and His disciples rebuked those that brought them. They thought Jesus had greater work: teaching, healing, walking on toward Jerusalem. Jesus was much displeased. He said, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God. Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein. He took them up in His arms, put His hands upon them, and blessed them. Matthew says He said, Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven. He did not wait until they were older, or quieter, or more useful. He wanted them near, with their small hands and their whole trust. The kingdom is not for people who have grown too important to be held.
“Suffer the little children to come unto me.” Mark 10:14.
You can come to Jesus even with crayons in your hand.
hear.daniel-lions:
A den of lions. Night. Daniel is there because he would not stop praying to God.
Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes. They sought to find occasion against him, but could find none, except concerning the law of his God. They tricked the king into a writing: whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of the king, shall be cast into the den of lions. When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house, his windows open toward Jerusalem, and kneeled three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. They found him, and the king, sore displeased, commanded, and they brought Daniel and cast him into the den. The king said, Thy God whom thou servest continually, He will deliver thee. A stone was laid, and sealed. The king passed the night fasting. In the morning he cried, O Daniel, is thy God able to deliver thee from the lions? Daniel said, My God hath sent His angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me. Daniel was taken up, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.
“My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths.” Daniel 6:22.
God is with you when you are afraid.
hear.empty-tomb:
Early, the first day of the week. It is still gray. Women who loved Jesus walk toward a tomb with spices.
Jesus had been crucified. Joseph of Arimathaea had laid His body in a new sepulchre, hewn out of the rock, and rolled a great stone to the door. They had even set a watch. When the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the sepulchre. There was a great earthquake. The angel of the Lord descended from heaven, rolled back the stone, and sat upon it. His countenance was like lightning. The keepers did shake and became as dead men. The angel said unto the women, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified. He is not here: for He is risen, as He said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay. Then go quickly, and tell His disciples that He is risen from the dead. They departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy, and did run to bring His disciples word. Jesus met them, saying, All hail. They held Him by the feet, and worshipped Him.
“He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.” Matthew 28:6.
Jesus is alive.
hear.feeding-5000:
A desert place. Evening coming on. A great multitude has followed Jesus, and they have nothing to eat.
Jesus went forth, saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and He healed their sick. When it was evening, His disciples said, This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages and buy themselves victuals. Jesus said, They need not depart; give ye them to eat. They say unto Him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes. There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many? Jesus said, Bring them hither to me. He commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass. He took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, He blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to His disciples, and the disciples to the multitude. They did all eat, and were filled. They took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full. They that had eaten were about five thousand men, beside women and children.
“And they did all eat, and were filled.” Matthew 14:20.
Jesus provides more than enough.
hear.jesus-storm:
A ship on the sea at night. Wind. Waves beating in. The disciples are afraid they will perish, and Jesus is asleep.
The same day, when the even was come, Jesus saith unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side. When they had sent away the multitude, they took Him even as He was in the ship. And there were also with Him other little ships. There arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. He was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow. They awake Him, and say unto Him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? He arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And He said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith? And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him? They had seen Him heal and teach. Now they saw that the sea itself knew His voice. The One who slept in their boat is Lord over the storm that filled it.
“Peace, be still.” Mark 4:39.
Jesus is Lord over the storm.
hear.good-samaritan:
A road from Jerusalem to Jericho. A man has fallen among thieves. He is stripped, wounded, and left half dead.
A certain priest came down that way, and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side. A Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side. But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, and went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him. On the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee. Jesus asked, Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves? He said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus, Go, and do thou likewise.
“Go, and do thou likewise.” Luke 10:37.
Love your neighbor with real help.
hear.prodigal-son:
A far country, then a road home. A younger son has taken his share and wasted it.
A certain man had two sons. The younger said, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. Not many days after, he gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. When he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine, and he began to be in want. He joined himself to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed swine. He would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him. When he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee. He arose, and came to his father. When he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. The son began his confession. The father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: and bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry.
“For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.” Luke 15:24.
The Father runs to welcome home.
hear.walks-on-water:
The fourth watch of the night. The ship is in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves. The wind is contrary.
Jesus had gone up into a mountain apart to pray. The ship was now in the midst of the sea. In the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid. Peter answered, Lord, if it be Thou, bid me come unto Thee on the water. Jesus said, Come. When Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, Lord, save me. Immediately Jesus stretched forth His hand, and caught him, and said, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? When they were come into the ship, the wind ceased. They that were in the ship came and worshipped Him, saying, Of a truth Thou art the Son of God.
“Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.” Matthew 14:27.
Keep your eyes on Jesus.
hear.zacchaeus:
Jericho. A crowded road. A short man cannot see Jesus for the press, so he runs ahead and climbs a sycomore tree.
Jesus entered and passed through Jericho. Behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich. He sought to see Jesus who He was, and could not for the press, because he was little of stature. He ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see Him: for He was to pass that way. When Jesus came to the place, He looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house. He made haste, and came down, and received Him joyfully. When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That He was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner. Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord, Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold. Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house.
“For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.” Luke 19:10.
Jesus knows your name.
hear.woman-at-well:
Samaria. Jacob’s well. About the sixth hour. Jesus is wearied with His journey and sits on the well.
There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water. Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink. His disciples were gone away unto the city to buy meat. Then saith the woman, How is it that Thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans. Jesus answered, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of Him, and He would have given thee living water. The woman saith, Sir, Thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. Jesus said, Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: but whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst. He told her of her life. She perceived He was a prophet. He said, I that speak unto thee am He. The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city, and saith to the men, Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?
“Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst.” John 4:14.
Jesus offers living water.
hear.ruth-naomi:
The road from Moab toward Bethlehem. Three women have known death. Naomi tells her daughters in law to go home.
Elimelech had gone into the country of Moab with Naomi and their two sons, because of a famine. The sons married Orpah and Ruth, then the men died. Naomi arose with her daughters in law, that she might return to Bethlehem. She said, Go, return each to her mother’s house: the LORD deal kindly with you. Orpah kissed her mother in law, but Ruth clave unto her. Naomi said, Behold, thy sister in law is gone back. Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God. Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried. When she saw that she was stedfastly minded to go with her, she left speaking unto her. So they two went until they came to Bethlehem, in the beginning of barley harvest.
“Whither thou goest, I will go.” Ruth 1:16.
Loyal love is a quiet strength.
hear.lazarus:
Bethany, nigh unto Jerusalem. A house in grief. A tomb with a stone. Lazarus, whom Jesus loved, has been dead four days.
Lazarus was sick. His sisters Mary and Martha sent unto Jesus, saying, Lord, behold, he whom Thou lovest is sick. When Jesus heard that, He said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God. He abode two days still in the same place, then said, Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep. Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead. When Jesus came, He found that he had lain in the grave four days already. Martha said, Lord, if Thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again. Martha saith, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Jesus said, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live. Mary came, fell down at His feet, and wept. When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, He groaned in the spirit, and was troubled, and said, Where have ye laid him? Jesus wept. He cometh to the grave. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it. Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. He lifted up His eyes, and said, Father, I thank Thee that Thou hast heard me. He cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes.
“I am the resurrection, and the life.” John 11:25.
Jesus’ word calls the dead, and they hear Him.
hear.lost-sheep:
Hill country. A hundred sheep. Evening coming. One is missing, and the Shepherd will not call ninety-nine enough.
Then drew near unto Him all the publicans and sinners for to hear Him. And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them. And He spake this parable unto them, saying, What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? He does not wait until morning if it is convenient. He goes after that which is lost, until he find it. When he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing. He does not drive the tired sheep home with a stick. He carries it. When he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost. I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance. Jesus also said, I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. The search is not a scolding. It is love that will not leave the one in the dark.
“Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.” Luke 15:6.
The Shepherd comes for the one.
hear.jairus-daughter:
A house that has gone quiet. People are weeping. They say a little girl of twelve years is dead.
There cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name. When he saw Jesus, he fell at His feet, and besought Him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray Thee, come and lay Thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live. Jesus went with him. Much people followed. While He yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue’s house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further? As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, He saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe. He suffered no man to follow Him, save Peter, and James, and John. He cometh to the house, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly. When He was come in, He saith, Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth. They laughed Him to scorn. When He had put them all out, He taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with Him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying. He took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise. Straightway the damsel arose, and walked. They were astonished with a great astonishment. He charged them straitly that no man should know it, and commanded that something should be given her to eat.
“Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.” Mark 5:41.
Jesus speaks, and a child lives.
hear.blind-man:
A roadside. A man who has never seen light. Neighbors will argue later about how it happened.
As Jesus passed by, He saw a man which was blind from his birth. His disciples asked, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind? Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him. When He had thus spoken, He spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and He anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay, and said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam. He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing. The neighbours said, Is not this he that sat and begged? Some said, This is he: others said, He is like him: but he said, I am he. They brought him to the Pharisees. They asked how he had received his sight. He said, A man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes. They reviled him. He answered, Whether He be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see. Jesus heard that they had cast him out. When He had found him, He said, Dost thou believe on the Son of God? He answered, Who is He, Lord, that I might believe on Him? Jesus said, Thou hast both seen Him, and it is He that talketh with thee. And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped Him.
“Lord, I believe.” John 9:38.
Jesus opens eyes and hearts.
hear.fishers-of-men:
The sea of Galilee. Nets. Ordinary work. Jesus is walking by the water, and the night’s fishing has failed.
Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. He saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. They straightway left their nets, and followed Him. Going on from thence, He saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them. They immediately left the ship and their father, and followed Him. Luke tells more. Jesus entered Simon’s ship, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. He sat down, and taught the people out of the ship. When He had left speaking, He said, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught. Simon said, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at Thy word I will let down the net. They inclosed a great multitude of fishes, and their net brake. They beckoned unto their partners. Simon Peter fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord. Jesus said, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men. They forsook all, and followed Him. He did not first call kings from palaces. He called men whose hands smelled like fish.
“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Matthew 4:19.
Jesus calls ordinary people.
hear.wedding-cana:
Cana of Galilee. A marriage. The mother of Jesus is there, and Jesus is called, and His disciples. Then the wine fails.
The third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee. When they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto Him, They have no wine. Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come. His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever He saith unto you, do it. There were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece. Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. They filled them up to the brim. He saith, Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was, he called the bridegroom, and saith, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now. This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth His glory; and His disciples believed on Him.
“This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee.” John 2:11.
Jesus turns need into joy.
hear.mustard-seed:
A field. A seed so small you could lose it between your fingers. Jesus is talking about the kingdom of heaven.
He put forth a parable unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof. Another parable spake He: The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened. Later the disciples said, Lord, increase our faith. And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you. The kingdom does not begin looking large. It begins looking like almost nothing — a seed, a pinch of leaven, a small yes — then God grows it until there is room for others to rest in its shade. Small is not the same as nothing, not in His hand.
“The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed.” Matthew 13:31.
Small faith in a great God can grow.
hear.the-sower:
A path, stones, thorns, and a field of good ground. A sower is walking, throwing seed with his hand.
Behold, a sower went forth to sow. When he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up. Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth, and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: and when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. Some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them. But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold. Jesus explained. The seed is the word of God. Those by the way side hear, then the devil taketh away the word. The stony ground hear with joy, but have no root, and in time of temptation fall away. The thorns are cares and riches and pleasures of this life. The good ground are they which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
“He that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it.” Matthew 13:23.
Ask God for a heart that keeps His Word.
hear.triumphal-entry:
The road down the mount of Olives into Jerusalem. Coats on the ground. Branches. A King coming, not on a war-horse.
When they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and were come to Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples, saying, Go into the village over against you, and ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me. This was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass. The disciples went, and did as Jesus commanded them, and brought the ass, and the colt, and put on them their clothes, and they set Him thereon. A very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way. The multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest. When He was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this? The multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.
“Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.” Matthew 21:9.
The King comes in peace.
hear.lost-coin:
A house at night. Ten pieces of silver. One is gone. A woman will not rest until she finds it.
Jesus drew near unto publicans and sinners to hear Him, and the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them. So He spake three parables of lost things found: a sheep, a coin, a son. What woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it? Ten pieces was not a toy. It was her living, maybe her dowry, counted and kept. She does not say nine is enough. She lights a candle because the house is dim. She sweeps because the coin is small and can hide in dust. She seeks diligently, not once around the room. When she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost. Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth. Heaven does not shrug at one missing. The search is careful. The joy is loud when the lost is found.
“Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.” Luke 15:9.
Heaven rejoices when the lost is found.
hear.healing-paralytic:
Capernaum. A house so full no one can get in at the door. Four friends will not turn back.
They brought to Him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed. When they could not come nigh unto Him for the press, they uncovered the roof where He was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay. When Jesus saw their faith, He said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee. Certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth. Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts? Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith He to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house. He arose, and departed to his house. When the multitude saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men.
“Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.” Matthew 9:2.
Jesus forgives and heals.
hear.good-shepherd:
Pasture. A fold. Sheep that know a voice. Jesus is talking about Himself.
Jesus said, I am the door of the sheep. All that ever came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them. I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly. I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. He that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth. I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine. As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep. Other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd. David had sung, The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: He leadeth me beside the still waters.
“I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.” John 10:11.
The Good Shepherd knows His sheep, and He stays.
hear.feeding-4000:
Another hillside. Another crowd. They have been with Jesus three days, and they have nothing left to eat.
Jesus called His disciples unto Him, and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat: and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way. His disciples say unto Him, Whence should we have so much bread in the wilderness, as to fill so great a multitude? Jesus saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? They said, Seven, and a few little fishes. He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground. He took the seven loaves and the fishes, and gave thanks, and brake them, and gave to His disciples, and the disciples to the multitude. They did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full. They that did eat were four thousand men, beside women and children. He sent away the multitude, and took ship. He had already fed five thousand. He did not grow tired of hungry people. He had compassion again.
“I have compassion on the multitude.” Matthew 15:32.
Jesus cares, and He feeds again.
hear.wise-foolish-builders:
Two houses. One on rock. One on sand. Rain is coming, and flood, and wind, and both men heard the same words.
Jesus had been teaching on the mount: the poor in spirit, the peacemakers, the secret place of prayer, the beam in thine own eye, the strait gate. He ended with this. Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock. And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it. And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at His doctrine: for He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes. Both men heard. Only one did. The storm did not create the difference. The storm told the truth about the foundation that was already there.
“Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.” Matthew 7:24.
Hearing is not enough. Do His words.
hear.the-talents:
A man travelling into a far country. He calls his own servants, and delivers unto them his goods.
Unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey. He that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents. He that had received two, he also gained other two. But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money. After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them. He that had received five talents brought other five, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more. His lord said, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord. He that had received two heard the same welcome. Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man… and I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth. His lord answered, Thou wicked and slothful servant. Thou oughtest to have put my money to the exchangers. Take therefore the talent from him. For unto every one that hath shall be given. The gift was never too small to use.
“Well done, thou good and faithful servant.” Matthew 25:21.
Faithful with a little matters to the Lord.
hear.persistent-widow:
A city. A judge who fears not God, neither regards man. A widow who will not stop coming.
Jesus spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint. There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man. There was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary. He would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man; yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me. The Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith. And shall not God avenge His own elect, which cry day and night unto Him, though He bear long with them? I tell you that He will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall He find faith on the earth? If a hard judge yields to a widow’s knocking, how much more will God hear His children who keep praying.
“Men ought always to pray, and not to faint.” Luke 18:1.
Keep praying. Do not faint.
hear.healing-leper:
A road. A man full of leprosy. He is not supposed to come near, but he does.
There came a leper to Him, beseeching Him, and kneeling down to Him, and saying unto Him, If Thou wilt, Thou canst make me clean. Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth His hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean. As soon as He had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed. He straitly charged him, and forthwith sent him away; and saith unto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them. But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to Him from every quarter. The man came believing Jesus could. Jesus was willing.
“I will; be thou clean.” Mark 1:41.
Jesus is willing to make clean.
hear.joseph-coat:
Canaan. A family of twelve sons. One coat that shines, and brothers who cannot speak peaceably.
Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a coat of many colours. When his brethren saw that their father loved him more, they hated him. Joseph dreamed, and told them: their sheaves made obeisance to his sheaf; the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to him. They hated him yet more for his dreams and for his words. Israel sent him from the vale of Hebron to see whether it was well with his brethren. They saw him afar off, and before he came near they conspired against him. They stripped him of his coat, and cast him into a pit. There was no water in it. Then they sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver, and they brought him into Egypt. They killed a kid of the goats, dipped the coat in the blood, and brought it to their father. Jacob knew it, and mourned. But the LORD was with Joseph in Egypt, in the house of Potiphar, and later even in the prison. Years later Joseph would say to those same brothers what they meant for evil, God meant for good, to save much people alive.
“But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.” Genesis 50:20.
God can use hard days for good.
hear.joseph-dreams:
Egypt. A prison, then a palace. Two dreams in the night, and a man who will not take the glory.
Joseph had been sold, then falsely accused, and put in the prison where the king’s prisoners were bound. The LORD was with him there. Pharaoh’s butler and baker dreamed. Joseph said, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you. He told the butler he would be restored in three days, and the baker that he would not. It came to pass as Joseph had said. The butler forgot him two full years. Then Pharaoh dreamed of seven well favoured kine, and seven lean that ate them; and of seven full ears, and seven thin. None of the magicians could interpret. Then the butler remembered Joseph. They brought him hastily out of the dungeon. Pharaoh said, I have heard that thou canst understand a dream to interpret it. Joseph answered, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace. The seven good are seven years of plenty. The seven lean are seven years of famine. Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and let him gather food. Pharaoh said, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is? He set Joseph over all the land of Egypt. The famine came. Joseph opened the storehouses, and people were saved, including his own family when they came down from Canaan.
“It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.” Genesis 41:16.
God can turn sorrow into saving.
hear.burning-bush:
The backside of the desert, near the mountain of God, even Horeb. A shepherd’s flock. A bush that burns and is not consumed.
Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law. The angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush. He looked, and behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed. Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight. When the LORD saw that he turned aside, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I. God said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground. I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Moses hid his face. The LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry. I am come down to deliver them, and to bring them unto a land flowing with milk and honey. Come now, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh. Moses said, Who am I? And, When they shall say, What is His name? what shall I say? God said, I AM THAT I AM: Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you. Moses still feared his slow speech. God gave him Aaron his brother to speak, and a rod in his hand. Moses went.
“I AM THAT I AM.” Exodus 3:14.
God sees. God sends.
hear.jericho:
A walled city in the land God promised. Israel has crossed Jordan. Jericho is straitly shut up.
The LORD said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho. Ye shall compass the city, all ye men of war, and go round about the city once. Thus shalt thou do six days. Seven priests shall bear before the ark seven trumpets of rams’ horns. The seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow with the trumpets. When they make a long blast, and ye hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; and the wall of the city shall fall down flat. Joshua told the people, Ye shall not shout nor make any noise with your voice, until the day I bid you shout. They did as the LORD said. They rose early. They walked. The ark of the LORD compassed the city. On the seventh day they rose about the dawning, and compassed the city after the same manner seven times. Joshua said, Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city. The people shouted, the priests blew, and the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him. Rahab and her house were saved, as the spies had sworn. The LORD was with Joshua.
“The wall fell down flat.” Joshua 6:20.
God keeps His word.
hear.gideon-fleece:
A threshing floor at night. A fleece of wool on the ground. Midian has worn Israel down, and a man named Gideon is afraid, and still God calls him.
The angel of the LORD appeared unto Gideon and said, The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour. Gideon said, If the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us? The LORD said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of Midian: have not I sent thee? Gideon answered, Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house. The LORD said, Surely I will be with thee. Gideon asked a sign. He put a fleece of wool in the floor, and said, If the dew be on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the earth beside, then shall I know. In the morning he wrung the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water. Then he asked again, Let it now be dry only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground let there be dew. God did so that night. Later God thinned Gideon’s army from twenty-two thousand to three hundred, lest Israel vaunt themselves. With trumpets and pitchers and lamps they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon, and the LORD set every man’s sword against his fellow. Israel was delivered.
“The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.” Judges 6:12.
God can use a small yes.
hear.samson:
The camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol. A child is promised, set apart to God, and later a strong man whose gift is not his own.
There was a man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. His wife was barren. The angel of the LORD told her she would bear a son. No razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb, and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines. The woman bare a son, and called his name Samson. The child grew, and the LORD blessed him, and the Spirit of the LORD began to move him. The Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent a young lion as he would have rent a kid. He judged Israel twenty years. Then he told the secret of his strength, and they shaved the seven locks of his head, and the LORD was departed from him. They bound him. In the prison he called on the LORD again. Samson said, O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray Thee, and strengthen me, I pray Thee, only this once. God heard. He took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, and the house fell. His strength had never been his hair alone. It was a gift from God, to be used for God.
“And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him.” Judges 14:6.
Strength is a gift to use for God.
hear.esther:
A palace in Shushan. A young Jewish woman is queen, and a wicked writing has gone out against her people.
King Ahasuerus reigned from India even unto Ethiopia. He made Esther queen, and she had not shewed her people nor her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her not to shew it. Haman the Agagite was promoted. Mordecai would not bow. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews. Lots were cast, and a decree was written to kill them. Mordecai rent his clothes. He sent word to Esther: Think not that thou shalt escape in the king’s house. Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this? Esther said, Gather all the Jews, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days. I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish. On the third day she put on her royal apparel and stood in the inner court. The king held out the golden sceptre. She invited the king and Haman to a banquet, then another. At the second she said, Let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request: for we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed. The king asked, Who is he? Esther said, The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman. Haman was hanged on the gallows he had made for Mordecai. Another writing went forth, and the Jews were delivered.
“If I perish, I perish.” Esther 4:16.
God can give quiet courage.
hear.fiery-furnace:
A plain in Babylon. A golden image. A furnace heated seven times hotter than it was wont to be heated.
Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits. A herald cried, At what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image. Whoso falleth not down shall be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego would not. Certain Chaldeans accused them. The king in rage said, Who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands? They answered, Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and He will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image. The furnace was heated seven times. Mighty men bound them and cast them in. The fire slew those men. Then the king was astonied, and said, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God. They came forth. Not a hair of their head was singed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them.
“Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us.” Daniel 3:17.
God can keep you in the fire.
hear.abraham-isaac:
A mountain in the land of Moriah. A father, his boy, wood for a fire, and a question about a lamb.
God did tempt Abraham, and said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of. Abraham rose up early in the morning, saddled his ass, took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood, and went. On the third day he saw the place afar off. He said to the young men, Abide ye here; I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you. Abraham took the wood and laid it upon Isaac, and he took the fire in his hand, and a knife. Isaac said, My father: behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering? Abraham said, My son, God will provide Himself a lamb. He built an altar, laid the wood, and bound Isaac. The angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven, Abraham, Abraham. Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me. Abraham lifted up his eyes, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns. He offered the ram. Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.
“God will provide himself a lamb.” Genesis 22:8.
God will provide.
hear.elijah-carmel:
Mount Carmel. Two altars. A waiting crowd. Baal’s prophets have cried all day, and there is no voice.
Ahab had done evil. Jezebel had cut off the prophets of the LORD. Elijah the Tishbite said, As the LORD God of Israel liveth, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word. In the third year the LORD sent him to Ahab. Elijah said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow Him: but if Baal, then follow him. He said, Call ye on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the LORD: and the God that answereth by fire, let Him be God. The prophets of Baal cried from morning even until noon, O Baal, hear us. There was neither voice, nor any to answer. They leaped upon the altar. Elijah mocked them. At evening he repaired the altar of the LORD with twelve stones. He put the wood, the bullock, and said, Fill four barrels with water, and pour it. Do it the second time. Do it the third time. The water ran about the altar and filled the trench. Elijah said, LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that Thou art God in Israel, and that I am Thy servant. Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water. When all the people saw it, they fell on their faces.
“The LORD, he is the God.” 1 Kings 18:39.
The LORD, He is the God.
hear.naaman:
Syria, then the Jordan. A captain, mighty and honourable, but a leper. A little maid from Israel knows where help is.
Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the LORD had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper. A little maid waited on Naaman’s wife. She said, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy. The king of Syria sent Naaman with a letter and ten talents of silver to the king of Israel. The king of Israel rent his clothes. Elisha sent, Let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel. Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the door. Elisha sent a messenger, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean. Naaman was wroth. He said, Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? His servants came near, and said, My father, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean? Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean. He returned to Elisha and said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel.
“His flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child.” 2 Kings 5:14.
Humble obedience meets mercy.
hear.boy-samuel:
Shiloh. The temple of the LORD at night. A lamp of God is not yet gone out. A boy is lying down to sleep.
The child Samuel ministered unto the LORD before Eli. The word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no open vision. The LORD called Samuel, and he answered, Here am I, and ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. Eli said, I called not; lie down again. The LORD called yet again, Samuel. He went to Eli again. Eli said, I called not, my son. The LORD called Samuel again the third time. Then Eli perceived that the LORD had called the child. Therefore Eli said, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if He call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, LORD; for Thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place. The LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for Thy servant heareth. The LORD told him what He would do in Israel. Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision, but Eli said, What is the thing that the LORD hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me. Samuel told him every whit. Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground. All Israel knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD.
“Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.” 1 Samuel 3:9.
God still speaks. We can listen.
hear.ten-lepers:
The way to Jerusalem. A village. Ten men stand afar off, because they are lepers, and they lift up their voices.
As Jesus went to Jerusalem, He passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee. As He entered into a certain village, there met Him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off: and they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us. When He saw them, He said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed. And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at His feet, giving Him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And He said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole. Ten were made clean on the road. One came back to the Giver. Jesus noticed both the healing and the missing thank-you.
“Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?” Luke 17:17.
Come back and give thanks.
hear.pharisee-tax-collector:
The temple. Two men go up to pray. One stands sure of himself. The other will not lift up his eyes.
Jesus spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others. Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican. The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank Thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. Jesus said, I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted. God was not impressed by the list. He heard the man who asked for mercy.
“God be merciful to me a sinner.” Luke 18:13.
Humble hearts are heard.
hear.widows-mite:
The temple treasury. People are casting in money. Some gifts sound heavy. One gift is two very small coins.
Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much. And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing. He called unto Him His disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: for all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. The rich gave from extra. She gave her living. Jesus did not measure the pile. He measured the cost, and the trust it took to let both coins go.
“She of her want did cast in all that she had.” Mark 12:44.
God sees what it cost.
hear.centurion-servant:
Capernaum. A house nearby. A servant is sick of the palsy, grievously tormented, and a soldier believes Jesus does not even have to come inside.
When Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto Him a centurion, beseeching Him, and saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented. Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him. The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed. For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it. When Jesus heard it, He marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel. And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour. Luke tells that the elders of the Jews came first, saying he was worthy, for he loved their nation and had built them a synagogue. The man himself said he was not worthy. Jesus praised the faith that trusted His word from a distance.
“Speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.” Matthew 8:8.
Great faith trusts Jesus’ word.
hear.abraham-sarah:
A tent under the stars. Two old people have waited a long time. God has made a promise they can hardly hold.
The LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and I will make of thee a great nation. He believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Years passed. Sarai was barren. God changed Abram’s name to Abraham, a father of many nations, and Sarai’s to Sarah. Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear? God said, Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son indeed; and thou shalt call his name Isaac. Later the LORD appeared by the oaks, and Sarah heard in the tent door. She laughed within herself. The LORD said, Wherefore did Sarah laugh? Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son. The LORD visited Sarah as He had said. Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken. Abraham called his name Isaac. Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.
“Is any thing too hard for the LORD?” Genesis 18:14.
Nothing is too hard for the Lord.
hear.elisha-oil:
A small house. Empty jars. A widow of a prophet, and two sons about to be taken for debt.
Now there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant did fear the LORD: and the creditor is come to take unto him my two sons to be bondmen. Elisha said, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil. Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few. And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full. So she went from him, and shut the door. Her sons brought the vessels to her, and she poured out. And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed. Then she came and told the man of God. He said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest. The little she had was enough in God’s hand, as long as there was an empty vessel to fill.
“Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.” 2 Kings 4:3.
God fills empty vessels.
hear.hannah-samuel:
Shiloh. The temple. A woman is praying, and her lips move, but her voice is not heard.
Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none. Year by year, when they went up to the house of the LORD, Peninnah provoked her. Hannah wept, and did not eat. Elkanah said, Hannah, why weepest thou? am not I better to thee than ten sons? Hannah rose up, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore. She vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if Thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of Thine handmaid, and remember me, and give unto Thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life. Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple. He thought she was drunken, because she spake in her heart; only her lips moved. Hannah said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD. Eli said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition. She went her way, and her countenance was no more sad. In process of time Hannah bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD. When she had weaned him, she brought him to the house of the LORD, and said, For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition which I asked of Him: therefore also I have lent him to the LORD.
“For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition.” 1 Samuel 1:27.
God hears a poured-out soul.
hear.david-jonathan:
A field, a palace, a covenant. Two friends whose souls are knit, while a king’s jealousy grows.
When David had made an end of speaking unto Saul after Goliath, the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. Saul took David that day. Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul. Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle. David went out whithersoever Saul sent him, and behaved himself wisely. Saul became David’s enemy continually. Jonathan told David, Saul my father seeketh to kill thee: now therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself until the morning. Jonathan spake good of David unto Saul, and Saul hearkened. Later Jonathan went to David in the wood, and strengthened his hand in God, and said, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee. They made a covenant again before the LORD. True friendship did not keep the throne. It kept faith, even when it cost a prince his own place.
“The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David.” 1 Samuel 18:1.
True friendship is loyal.
hear.rich-young-ruler:
A road. A young man with many possessions runs and kneels. He wants eternal life, and still his things hold his heart.
When Jesus was gone forth into the way, there came one running, and kneeled to Him, and asked Him, Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life? Jesus said, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God. Thou knowest the commandments. He answered, Master, all these have I observed from my youth. Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me. And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions. Jesus looked round about, and saith unto His disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God! The disciples were astonished. Jesus said, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible. Peter began to say, Lo, we have left all, and have followed Thee. Jesus promised a hundredfold, with persecutions, and in the world to come eternal life. The young man had kept a list. He would not let go of the thing that sat on the throne of his heart.
“Come and follow me.” Matthew 19:21.
Follow Jesus above all.
hear.pearl-great-price:
A merchant among pearls. He has seen many that were good. Then he finds one that is worth selling everything.
Jesus sat by the sea and taught in parables. Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field. Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls: who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it. He was already looking. He already knew the worth of pearls. This one was different. He did not add it to a collection. He sold all that he had. The kingdom is not a small extra to keep if it is convenient. It is the one thing so good that everything else can go, and the heart is not cheated.
“The kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls.” Matthew 13:45.
The kingdom is worth everything.
hear.withered-hand:
A synagogue on the sabbath. A man whose hand is withered. Some watch Jesus, not to learn, but to accuse.
Jesus went into their synagogue: and, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. They asked Him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse Him. He said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. Then saith He to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other. Mark says Jesus looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts. The Pharisees went out, and held a council against Him, how they might destroy Him. The man did what he could not do until Jesus spoke. The hand that could not work was made whole in the house of God, on the day some men thought help should wait.
“Stretch forth thine hand.” Matthew 12:13.
Jesus restores what is broken.
hear.unforgiving-servant:
A king’s court. A debt so large it cannot be paid. Mercy is given, then refused to a neighbour.
Peter came to Jesus and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven. Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account of his servants. One was brought which owed him ten thousand talents. He had not to pay. His lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had. The servant fell down, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all. Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt. The same servant went out, and found one of his fellowservants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest. His fellowservant fell down and besought him. He would not, but cast him into prison. When his fellowservants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and told their lord. Then his lord said, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee? And his lord was wroth. So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.
“Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant?” Matthew 18:33.
Forgiven people forgive.
hear.boy-david:
Bethlehem. A field of sheep. Brothers who look tall and strong stand before the prophet, and God is looking somewhere else.
The LORD said unto Samuel, Fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Bethlehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons. Samuel came, and the elders trembled. He sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice. When Eliab came, Samuel looked on his countenance, and on the height of his stature, and said, Surely the LORD’s anointed is before Him. But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart. Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. Samuel said, The LORD hath not chosen these. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep. Samuel said, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he come hither. He was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance. The LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he. Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward.
“The LORD looketh on the heart.” 1 Samuel 16:7.
God looks on the heart.
hear.elijah-ravens:
A hidden brook named Cherith, before Jordan. No rain. A prophet waiting, and birds that should not be bringing bread.
Elijah the Tishbite said unto Ahab, As the LORD God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word. And the word of the LORD came unto him, saying, Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith, that is before Jordan. And it shall be, that thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there. So he went and did according unto the word of the LORD. The ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook. And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land. Then the word of the LORD came, saying, Arise, get thee to Zarephath. God had already named the next place, and the next way to feed him. Before the widow, before Carmel, God kept His prophet alive with a brook and with birds, in a quiet place nobody would have chosen.
“I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.” 1 Kings 17:4.
God provides in quiet ways.
hear.writing-on-wall:
Babylon. A loud feast. Gold and silver vessels that belong in the house of God. Then fingers of a man’s hand, writing on the plaster.
Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand. He commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem, that the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, might drink therein. They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone. In the same hour came forth fingers of a man’s hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king’s palace. The king’s countenance was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, so that the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another. The wise men could not read the writing. The queen remembered Daniel. Daniel was brought. He would not take the gifts. He said, Thou hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven. The vessels were brought, and the God in whose hand thy breath is, thou hast not glorified. This is the writing: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. MENE: God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it. TEKEL: Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting. PERES: Thy kingdom is divided. That night Belshazzar was slain, and Darius the Median took the kingdom.
“Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.” Daniel 5:27.
God weighs the heart.
hear.ruth-boaz:
Bethlehem at barley harvest. A field that belongs to a kinsman. A young woman from Moab is gleaning behind the reapers.
Naomi had come home empty, and Ruth her daughter in law with her. Ruth said, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. Her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech. Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said unto the reapers, The LORD be with you. He asked, Whose damsel is this? The servant told him she was the Moabitess that came back with Naomi. Boaz said unto Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field, but abide here fast by my maidens. Have I not charged the young men that they shall not touch thee? And when thou art athirst, go unto the vessels. Ruth fell on her face and said, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, seeing I am a stranger? Boaz answered, It hath fully been shewed me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law. The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust. At mealtime he said, Come thou hither, and eat. He commanded handfuls of purpose for her. Later Boaz went to the gate, and the near kinsman would not redeem. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech’s, and took Ruth to be his wife. The LORD gave her a son, Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David.
“The LORD recompense thy work.” Ruth 2:12.
Kindness opens a future of hope.
hear.jesus-baptism:
The Jordan. Crowds coming to John. Then Jesus stepping into the water, though John does not feel worthy.
In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, and saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. John said, I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but He that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear. Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. But John forbad Him, saying, I have need to be baptized of Thee, and comest Thou to me? And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered Him. And Jesus, when He was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto Him, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon Him: and lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. John had pointed to the Lamb of God. Heaven said the same with a voice and with a dove.
“This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” Matthew 3:17.
This is My beloved Son.
hear.emmaus-road:
A long road to a village called Emmaus, about threescore furlongs from Jerusalem. It is the third day. Two friends are sad, and talking of all these things which had happened.
Jesus Himself drew near, and went with them. But their eyes were holden that they should not know Him. He said, What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad?
